title: Adaptive error classification and actionable summaries across SDKs
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Create a cross-language error classification layer and developer-facing summaries so Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs provide consistent error codes, short actionable messages, and structured retry/resume hints for both unary and streaming calls.
background: Current SDK error surfaces vary: some languages return rich typed exceptions, others return code strings. Streaming interruptions are inconsistently resumable and retry guidance is buried in docs. This causes user confusion and increases support load for transient failures, backpressure, and idempotency mistakes.
proposal: Introduce an SDK-agnostic ErrorKind enum (TRANSPORT, TIMEOUT, RATE_LIMIT, QUOTA, MODEL_DEGRADED, INVALID_INPUT, AUTH, PERMISSION, INTERNAL) mapped to language-specific exception types.
Attach a short human-friendly summary (one sentence) and a 1-2 line next-action hint to every SDK error instance; examples: 'Request timed out — try increasing client timeout or reducing batch size.'

Standardize structured metadata fields on errors: code (string), kind (ErrorKind), retry_hint (none|retryable|idempotent-retry), resume_token (opaque string when streaming can resume), vendor_tid (trace id for debugging).

Streaming: implement resume_token generation on server side and expose resume_token on stream interruptions; SDKs should expose resume() helper that accepts token and replays client-side state where possible.
Retries: provide unified retry policy metadata per error (backoff_base_ms, max_retries_recommended) and surface a high-level SDK policy that respects server retry_hint and client override.
Telemetry and docs: ensure every error emits a stable error_code (e.g., SDK_ERR_0201) that links to internal docs with repros, mitigations, and common root causes.

Backwards compatibility: keep existing exception class names but attach the structured metadata to avoid breaking callers that inspect error strings. Ship opt-in feature flag for strict typed errors in next major SDK bump.
acceptance_criteria: All three SDKs (python, typescript, go) surface error.code and error.kind on exceptions or error objects for unary calls
Streaming interruptions include resume_token when the server supports resume; resume_token is opaque and present in >=95% of resumable disconnects in test harness
SDKs expose a helper to translate error into a short actionable message and recommended action string
Retry logic reads retry_hint and respects server-provided backoff_base_ms and max_retries_recommended by default; tests demonstrate configuration overrides
Integration test harness (recorded in CI) asserts stable numeric error_code strings and maps them to internal docs links
Migration guide published with examples and runtime toggle to enable strict typed exceptions
tasks: Design: finalize ErrorKind enum, code namespace, and metadata contract (doc: /design/sdk-error-contract.md)
Runtime: add error metadata envelope in server responses and support resume_token generation (infra change)
Python SDK: implement Exception subclasses with .code/.kind/.retry_hint and resume helper
TS SDK: implement Error subclass and Result-like error object for callback/streaming ergonomics
Go SDK: implement typed error interfaces and helper functions to extract metadata
E2E tests: extend streaming harness to simulate resumable disconnect and validate resume_token behavior
Docs: publish migration guide, examples for idempotent retries, and sample code for resume flows
Telemetry: add stable error_code to logs and link to internal troubleshooting pages

tests: Unit: ensure exceptions include code/kind/ retry_hint fields and stringifies cleanly
Integration: streaming harness simulates disconnects and validates resume() replays state
Chaos: introduce transient TCP resets in CI and assert client-side retry behavior honors retry_hint
Compatibility: run existing customers' SDK integration tests to ensure no API breakage
notes: We intentionally separate short actionable message from long troubleshooting doc to keep UX concise in logs and consoles
resume_token is intentionally opaque to avoid coupling SDKs to server internals; SDKs must not attempt to decode it
We will keep backwards-compatible string error messages but recommend consumers migrate to .code + .kind for programmatic handling
